entries.summary: Checker moved from per-feature inner-loop review to one final acceptance batch after the complete delivery is handed off.
entries.why: The repository owner explicitly requested that checker check only the last step after everything has been handed over. Per-feature checker hops interrupted delivery order and judged features before downstream integration existed.
entries.targetImpact: readyForCheck now means a complete handoff that unlocks dependent implementation, not acceptance. The router dispatches checker only when every non-blocked open feature is readyForCheck. Rejection clears the affected handoff and delivery resumes; another checker turn waits for a complete batch again. run-loop no longer mechanically promotes claims before checker.
mergeActions: Refresh route.mjs and run-loop.mjs together so handoff-aware dependency eligibility and final checker routing cannot drift.
Merge project-specific maker/checker prompts while preserving the final-batch timing contract.
Regenerate runtime agents from agents.manifest.json after prompt changes.
Preserve project feature state; existing readyForCheck claims become delivery handoffs and will be reviewed together once the remaining work is handed off.

The loop's `--headless` flag remains as a human-supervision switch for CI/cron; it no longer means Kiro headless transport. Claude and Codex dispatch are unchanged.
mergeActions: Refresh loop/dispatch.mjs and install the new skill-owned tools/kiro-acp-dispatch.mjs together; dispatch points at that file immediately.
Keep project prompts and agent configs; the ACP process still selects the same generated Kiro role with --agent.
Do not translate --headless into a transport choice: it controls only between-iteration checkpoints.

Regenerate runtime agent files from agents.manifest.json.

entries.summary: Fresh scaffolds place harness state, machinery and documentation under root/harness.
entries.why: Scattering tools, prompts, loop state, skills and harness documentation across the product root made experimental files hard to identify and remove; ignoring them hid all change visibility.
entries.targetImpact: Root retains only AGENTS.md and runtime-mandated discovery adapters. The harness directory stays visible to Git, installation.json identifies changes without a product commit, and ignored harness/env/local.json contains redacted machine-specific configuration.
mergeActions: Create the contained harness home and move only classified harness-owned files; do not move product-owned docs or tools by directory name alone.
Keep root runtime adapters generated from harness/agents.manifest.json.
Rewrite harness-owned references in prompts and docs to their harness/ paths; a physical move without instruction migration is incomplete.
Run the router relative to its contained home while resolving generated runtime agents at project root.
Capture local Java/Maven and Kubernetes selectors under harness/env; never copy API-key values into a tracked or checksummed artifact.
Retain the legacy layout until target-specific drift has been classified; this structural migration is a human-reviewed merge.

entries.summary: `designer` and `design-reviewer` are retired and merged into one `design-facilitator` agent; the auto-reject loop between them is replaced by a human-authored `loop/design-approval.json`.
entries.why: designer/design-reviewer could reject and re-dispatch each other with no human in the loop, and a design that changed even slightly between rounds reset the one-bounded-retry escalation counter, so rejection could cycle indefinitely — every round a paid session, and neither agent had the business context to know when a design was actually done. Full incident: docs/reference/graph.md row 11.
entries.targetImpact: route.mjs no longer dispatches design-reviewer or bounces a rejected design back to designer; any design revision without an approval matching its exact digest routes straight to a human, always. loop/design-review.json is no longer produced or read. A design edited after approval — even by one line — silently invalidates the approval (digest mismatch), which is intentional: there is no partial-credit 'still basically approved' state.
mergeActions: If prompts/designer.md or prompts/design-reviewer.md were customized here, port the customization into prompts/design-facilitator.md by hand — a diff cannot merge two files into one.

Delete the now-orphaned prompts/designer.md and prompts/design-reviewer.md, and their .kiro/.claude/.codex generated files, once customizations are ported — the file-diff refresh does not remove files that no longer exist in the canonical templates, only agents.manifest.json's newAgents/retiredAgents comparison surfaces that they are gone.

If a feature is mid-flight in the old cycle (a NEEDS DESIGN: marker already answered, or a rejected loop/design-review.json sitting unresolved), resolve it under the old contract first, or explicitly re-open it: have a human review the current docs/design/*.md and write loop/design-approval.json before continuing.
Delete any lingering loop/design-review.json — it is not read by the new routing rules and its presence is misleading.
Regenerate every runtime from agents.manifest.json after the prompt merge.
verification: node loop/route.mjs --rules shows design-facilitator, not designer/design-reviewer, in the design-layer rows
an unapproved docs/design/*.md routes to human, never to an agent (node loop/route.mjs --json)

entries.summary: On kiro, orchestrator's generated config now declares the built-in `subagent` tool and a computed `toolsSettings.subagent.availableAgents` naming every other agent — enforcing 'never spawn the orchestrator itself' by config instead of prompt text alone.
entries.why: kiro-cli has a native in-session `subagent` tool (verified against kiro.dev's docs, not assumed) gated by `toolsSettings.subagent.availableAgents`/`.trustedAgents`, but this harness's manifest never declared either for orchestrator — so on kiro specifically, 'never spawn the orchestrator itself' (prompts/orchestrator.md, 'What you must not do') was purely prompt-only, the same unenforced-MUST-NOT gap verify-harness.mjs's `rules` gate already flags elsewhere.
entries.targetImpact: kiro's orchestrator.json gains `tools: [..., "subagent"]` and `toolsSettings.subagent.availableAgents` listing every other manifest agent (computed by gen-agents.mjs at generation time, so it never needs hand-updating when an agent is added or renamed). Claude Code and Codex are unaffected — no verified native in-session subagent mechanism is documented for them in this repo, so nothing changed there.
mergeActions: Add `subagentAllExceptSelf: true` and `"subagent"` in `tools` to this target's own orchestrator manifest entry — do not hand-list agent names; gen-agents.mjs computes the roster.

If this target's orchestrator entry was customized (a narrower `tools` list, a hand-written `toolsSettings`), merge rather than overwrite — `subagentAllExceptSelf` only adds a `subagent` sub-key, it does not touch `toolsSettings.write`.

entries.summary: `memory-consolidate.mjs` gains `--bootstrap`: it mines `feature_list.json` checkerNotes and `trace/trace.jsonl` blocked/REJECT events for a reason that recurred across >=2 features and isn't already written into `memory/**`, and lists it as a candidate. Also removed the empty, orphaned `memory/context-interviewer/` template dir left over from the interviewer-agent retirement (HI-052).
entries.why: A project that never wrote a memory entry does not start from zero knowledge — the raw material for a lesson (a checkerNotes reason a maker/checker kept re-hitting, a blocked reason that recurred) was already sitting in state files the harness already writes. Requiring someone to notice the pattern by eye before memory got its first real entry meant the mechanism only ever got exercised on projects mature enough to have already built the habit by hand.
entries.targetImpact: `tools/memory-consolidate.mjs --target . --bootstrap [--json]` is a new, additive CLI surface; the existing structural report (index budget, orphans, duplicates) is unchanged and still runs without `--bootstrap`. It never writes to `memory/**` itself — same report-not-rewrite division of labor the rest of the script already uses. `memory/context-interviewer/` (template only, never scaffolded into a real project) is gone; nothing reads it.
mergeActions: Copy the updated `tools/memory-consolidate.mjs` into the target as-is — it is additive (a new flag), so a local customization to the structural-report path is unaffected.
No action needed for the removed `memory/context-interviewer/` dir — it was never scaffolded into an existing target in the first place.

entries.summary: Every writing agent's prompt (maker, checker, feature-planner, test-designer, test-implementer, harness-setup, design-facilitator, orchestrator) now closes with an explicit, uniformly-worded Yes/No reflection gate before it stops, instead of a one-off sentence phrased differently per agent. `test-implementer` previously had no closing memory guidance at all — that gap is now closed too.
entries.why: `docs/reference/agent-memory.md` already named the `stop` hook's moment as 'the natural place to also prompt' this question, but the hook itself can only run a shell command (it fired `trace.mjs`'s `session-end` event and nothing else) — it cannot force an honest self-assessment. The enforceable half of that intention was always the prompt text, and it existed per-agent as loose prose an agent could skim past inside a longer numbered list, phrased slightly differently every time, which made it easy to treat as one more instruction rather than a forced branch to actually answer.
entries.targetImpact: Each agent prompt's memory-writing instruction is now a literal two-branch question ('did this run produce something the next run shouldn't have to rediscover? Yes -> write an entry. No -> nothing to write') instead of a single conditional sentence. The underlying trigger criteria (a non-obvious mistake, an approach that worked for a non-obvious reason, an ambiguity that was hard to call, etc.) are unchanged per agent — only the framing is uniform. No hook or tool behavior changed.
mergeActions: If a target customized the closing memory paragraph of any of these prompts, port the customization's specific trigger criteria into the new Yes/No framing by hand — a mechanical diff would overwrite the customization.
No tool, hook, or schema changed; this is prompt text only.

entries.summary: Two new MUST rules in docs/constraints.md: write progress.md/DECISIONS.md as short bullets not prose, and check the existing tools/*.mjs toolbox before writing a new script.
entries.why: Observed both problems in practice: progress.md entries drifting into essay-length prose, and ad-hoc one-off scripts/inline checks duplicating tools that already exist.
entries.targetImpact: docs/constraints.md gains two MUST rules, auto-loaded into every writing agent. No new gate, no new script — prompt-only fix.
mergeActions: Copy the two new bullets into the target's docs/constraints.md as-is.

entries.summary: 6 files (harness-cli.mjs, check-coverage.mjs, environment.mjs, init.mjs, loop/route.mjs, loop/dispatch.mjs) no longer infer 'contained layout' from directory name alone — a flat project named literally 'harness' was misdetected as contained, resolving PROJECT_ROOT one level too high.

entries.targetImpact: The heuristic now also requires the parent directory to have its own AGENTS.md (the thin pointer a contained scaffold writes) before treating a harness-named directory as contained. Only affects targets whose own directory happens to be named 'harness'.

entries.targetImpact: A feature from an unrelated subsystem no longer needs a citation just because some other docs/design/*.md elsewhere declares invariants. A feature that does cite a made-up invariant id is still caught (that check stayed global).
mergeActions: Copy the updated check-plan.mjs as-is; verify with skills/feature-planning/evals/run-fixtures.mjs (all 3 fixtures must still PASS).

entries.summary: docs/reference/graph.md's intro no longer asserts contained harness/ layout unconditionally.

entries.targetImpact: The intro paragraph now names both layouts. No path in the rest of the table changed.

entries.summary: approval-gate.mjs fires a best-effort OS notification the moment it writes a fresh approval request, so a headless run does not silently sit until timeout with nobody having seen it.
entries.why: Observed live: a headless run-loop.mjs sat at an approval gate with nobody watching that terminal. A safe timeout (APPROVAL_TIMEOUT_MIN) prevents an infinite hang, but auto-rejecting on a timeout nobody saw still spends the judgement this gate exists to get.
entries.targetImpact: macOS uses osascript, Windows uses the built-in WinRT toast APIs (no extra module), Linux uses notify-send. HARNESS_NOTIFY=0 opts out; HARNESS_NOTIFY_CMD overrides with any `cmd title message`. A missing/broken notifier never blocks or fails the gate — it degrades to prior behavior.
mergeActions: Copy the updated approval-gate.mjs as-is; no schema or CLI flag changed, only an additive notify() call.

entries.summary: New verify-harness.mjs gate state-log-prose: flags (warn) >=3 consecutive non-bulleted lines in progress.md/DECISIONS.md.
entries.why: docs/constraints.md already requires terse bullets there; nothing mechanical checked it. A crude structural proxy (no list marker) catches the common case without claiming real verbosity judgment.
entries.targetImpact: New warn-only finding id state-log-prose:<file>:<line>. No blocker, no schema change.
mergeActions: Copy the updated verify-harness.mjs as-is.

entries.summary: loop/route.mjs: the test-implementer rule and maker's unwritten-set filter now exclude status=blocked prove-features.
entries.why: HI-056, found live on examples/jdt-mcp-server: `open` deliberately includes blocked features for visibility, but a rule that DISPATCHES action must not act on one — a blocked feature re-matched every iteration (observed 19 times) instead of staying stopped for a human.
entries.targetImpact: A prove feature with status=blocked no longer triggers test-implementer, and no longer blocks an unrelated build feature via the unwritten-test check.
mergeActions: If a target hand-patched this locally (as examples/jdt-mcp-server had), the canonical version now matches — copy over the local patch without re-diffing it.

entries.summary: verify-harness.mjs's --promote no longer promotes a feature whose checkerNotes starts with REJECT, even if its old verification command still exits 0.
entries.why: HI-057, found live on examples/jdt-mcp-server: checker-prompt.md sets status back to in-progress on REJECT (so the router keeps offering it to the maker), which --promote could not distinguish from 'in-progress, never checked'. feat-lsp-client was rejected for lacking a real process-boundary oracle and was silently promoted to done on the next --promote pass anyway — a core-invariant violation ('only the checker sets done').
entries.targetImpact: promoteFeatures() adds one guard: skip if /^REJECT\b/ matches checkerNotes' first line (same marker convention route.mjs already uses for NEEDS DESIGN:/NEEDS RE-PLAN:).
mergeActions: Copy the updated verify-harness.mjs as-is.

Audit feature_list.json for any feature with status done/passing and checkerNotes starting with REJECT — that is exactly the corruption this fix prevents going forward, but an existing target may already carry one; revert its status to in-progress by hand.

entries.summary: Maker checkpoints no longer dispatch checker; readyForCheck now means a complete feature-level behavior with green verification and complete evidence, and attempts counts rejected review cycles.
entries.why: HI-058: run-loop.mjs unconditionally dispatched checker after every maker iteration and maker-prompt.md unconditionally set readyForCheck, so small partial advances paid for an independent review before there was a complete claim to falsify.
entries.targetImpact: A maker may commit several bounded checkpoints on one active feature with readyForCheck=false. run-loop.mjs skips checker until a complete claim is ready. Checker increments attempts on REJECT and blocks at maxAttempts; partial maker checkpoints no longer consume that budget.
mergeActions: Refresh the listed skill-owned files.
For existing feature rows, reinterpret attempts as prior rejected review cycles where history permits; do not mechanically retain counts known to represent maker checkpoints.
Do not set readyForCheck on partial work; leave the active feature false until its complete behavior and verification are green.

Existing Codex targets must refresh the generated hook and the four runtime tools together.
mergeActions: Refresh guard-write.mjs, hook-calibrate.mjs, codex-dispatch.mjs, verify-harness.mjs and loop/dispatch.mjs as one compatibility set.

mergeActions: Refresh loop-status.mjs and orchestrator.md together.
Preserve target-specific presentation wording, but retain the mandatory post-change progress line and fresh route lookup.

entries.summary: A typed, digest-bound reviewPacket is admitted before checker dispatch; structured checkerVerdict separates declared-contract misses from novel counterexamples.
entries.why: HI-061, observed on examples/jdt-mcp-server: 7 of 17 recent semantic verdicts were REJECT, with avoidable repeated gaps in returned cleanup, process teardown, live collection iteration, compound redundancy and real stdout. readyForCheck carried only prose evidence, so the checker had to rediscover whether the public rubric was complete.
entries.targetImpact: Every new readyForCheck submission must pass tools/review-contract.mjs. Missing fields produce SUBMISSION_INCOMPLETE, skip checker and leave attempts unchanged. Once a feature adopts reviewPacket, semantic reviews also record checkerVerdict; REJECT carries a violated reference, counterexample, reproduction, observation and exit criterion.
mergeActions: Refresh the listed skill-owned files as one protocol change.
Do not synthesize reviewPacket for historical done features. For the next maker submission, compute contractDigest with `node tools/review-contract.mjs <id> --json` and fill the public rubric.
Preserve checker independence: migrate actionable prose REJECT details into checkerVerdict, but do not publish private mutant implementations before review.

entries.summary: One feature's implementation step may now be built by several makers at once over disjoint file sets, with exactly one maker running the verification afterwards.
entries.why: WIP=1 bounds features, not files, so a step touching several independent modules was serialized for no reason — while the real hazard (two agents in one file, or two agents writing single-writer state) had no mechanical guard. tools/work-split.mjs supplies it: a plan is refused when its slices intersect by glob or on disk, when a slice reaches feature_list.json/progress.md/loop/**/memory/**, when a brief is too thin for a worker that has nobody to ask, or when the fan-in runs anything other than the feature's own verification.
entries.targetImpact: Optional capability; nothing changes for a target that never writes a plan. loop/route.mjs gains three implementation-layer rules and a mode field; the orchestrator gains one bounded exception to spawning a single child; the maker prompt gains slice-worker and integrator modes; guard-write.mjs confines a worker to its slice when HARNESS_SLICE is set; run-loop.mjs dispatches a fan-out headless (HARNESS_MAX_PARALLEL, default 4). Confinement is real only for workers started with loop/dispatch.mjs --slice on Claude Code or Codex; an in-session spawn cannot set per-child environment, and kiro has no PreToolUse hook at all.
mergeActions: Copy tools/work-split.mjs and create loop/work-split/ with its README; both are new, so no target content is at risk.

Take the three implementation-layer rules and the mode/slices output from the canonical route.mjs; a target that customized route.mjs keeps its own rules and gains these three immediately above the plain maker rule.

entries.summary: Four fixes drawn from reading every memory entry across the example projects: the memory schema is now checked, memory findings are grouped, duplicate detection compares bodies rather than exact wording, a blocked dependency is named where it dams open work, the review contract asks what a wrong implementation would still pass, and a prove feature whose own oracle is wrong finally has a node allowed to fix it.
entries.why: HI-068: agent-memory.md documents an entry frontmatter schema that nothing enforced, so on examples/jdt-mcp-server 61 of 71 entries had none, duplicate detection silently no-opped, memory-query.mjs returned '[?]' with empty hooks, and two maker entries five features apart recorded the identical root cause — the second costing a mutant round that read as 'all mutants survived'. The same tool emitted 66 identical warnings out of 68 findings, the wall AGENTS.md calls worse than no gate. HI-069: route.mjs's test-implementer rule keys on empty evidence, so a project that authors oracles before the implementation put every prove feature permanently out of the oracle layer's reach while the maker was forbidden to touch the test and the checker could not write it — no node could fix that file. HI-070: a blocked prove feature used as a stage gate turns its maxAttempts into the whole downstream branch's budget, and the only symptom was the router saying 'none routable'. HI-071: adversarialChecks had five keys and none asked the question a green run cannot answer for itself, which is what about twenty-five checker and maker memory entries are all separately about.
entries.targetImpact: memory-consolidate.mjs and environment.mjs gain findings/fields but change no behaviour a target depends on. loop/route.mjs gains one oracle-layer rule and a dependency-walk on the none-routable fallthrough. verify-harness.mjs gains the blocked-dependency-dam warn. tools/review-contract.mjs now REQUIRES adversarialChecks.discrimination as a sentence: any reviewPacket written before this upgrade becomes SUBMISSION_INCOMPLETE until the field is added, which is maker feedback and costs no checker attempt. The three prompts gain the NEEDS ORACLE FIX: contract.

Expect memory findings to appear on any target with real memory: missing frontmatter is pre-existing debt, not a regression, and the grouped counts are what make it readable.

entries.summary: Memory entries and index hooks are written in English, whatever language the rest of the project uses. Existing entries in another language stay as they are.
entries.why: Memory is not project prose: it is an operational record addressed to whichever agent runs next, in the same class as a log line or an identifier, and the reader is rarely the writer. A mixed-language index also costs the cheap skim the index exists to buy — examples/jdt-mcp-server had 43 of its index lines and 55 of its 81 entries in a second language. Deliberately a rule and not a gate: with the back catalogue frozen, a check would fire on 98 items forever with no action available, which is the wall AGENTS.md calls worse than no gate.
entries.targetImpact: Documentation only. references/agent-memory.md states the rule, and every memory/<agent>/MEMORY.md template repeats it where an agent will read it before writing. No existing entry is rewritten, and nothing fails because of one.
